name: Horde
summary: Across Kalimdor and Lordaeron, the Horde seeks survival and freedom under warchief thrall. Orcs, Darkspear trolls, and tauren share shamanic bonds, while the Forsaken keep an uneasy place among them. Old grievances and hostile neighbors test a people who prize strength, action, and honor over political maneuvering.

sections.title: A Reborn Union
sections.body:
The Horde that stands now has left behind the demonic army that crossed the Dark Portal in the First and Second Wars. After freeing his people from the Burning Legion, warchief thrall led the orcs across the Great Sea to Kalimdor.

There they sought a spiritual homeland shaped by ancestral traditions and honor. Along the way, Thrall formed lasting ties with Vol'jin's displaced Darkspear trolls and Cairne Bloodhoof's tauren. Together, they fought centaur and demonic incursions during the Third War.

sections.title: The Kalimdor Core
sections.body: In Kalimdor, the orcs founded Durotar and raised Orgrimmar as its fortress capital. They gave the Darkspear refuge on the nearby Echo Isles. Farther south, the nomadic tauren gathered across Mulgore's plains around Thunder Bluff under high chieftain cairne bloodhoof. These three peoples share shamanic reverence, a deep bond with nature, and the need to survive. Bloodshed and spiritual respect have bound them as family, not merely allies of convenience.

sections.title: An Alliance of Convenience
sections.body: Across the sea, in Lordaeron's ruined lands, lady sylvanas windrunner led the free-willed Forsaken out of the Scourge's grasp. Human factions and Scourge remnants still opposed them, so Sylvanas sought a place in the Horde. Tauren elders argued that the undead might yet be redeemed. Thrall accepted the Forsaken, giving the Horde a vital military outpost in the Eastern Kingdoms, though many in Kalimdor had misgivings.

sections.title: A Cold War
sections.body:
Thrall hopes to preserve peace with the Alliance, but the Old Horde's legacy still casts a shadow. To humans and dwarves, orcs remain bloodthirsty invaders, and the undead cannot be trusted.

Clashes over Ashenvale's vital lumber and skirmishes along territorial borders have left both factions in a tense, fragile cold war. Thrall directs campaigns against demon cults such as the Burning Blade to prove the Horde has broken with the Legion. Deep hatred still threatens to ignite all-out war at any spark.

faq.q: What is the difference between the Old Horde and the New Horde?
faq.answer: The Old Horde was a blood-crazed conquering host manipulated by the Burning Legion into invading Azeroth during the First and Second Wars. Founded by warchief thrall, the New Horde rejected demonic corruption and returned to ancestral shamanism. It became a defensive alliance of outcasts seeking survival, land, and spiritual renewal.

warchief thrall leads the Horde from the Valley of Wisdom in Orgrimmar. He directs its military and diplomacy, with counsel and leadership from high chieftain cairne bloodhoof of the tauren, Shadow Hunter Vol'jin of the Darkspear, and lady sylvanas windrunner of the Forsaken.

faq.q: Why are the Forsaken part of the Horde?
faq.answer: With hostile Alliance remnants and the Scourge surrounding them in Lordaeron, lady sylvanas windrunner sought allies for survival. Tauren elders argued that the Forsaken might yet be redeemed, and Thrall accepted them despite his reluctance. In return, the Horde gained a critical defensive foothold in the Eastern Kingdoms.

faq.q: Where is the capital of the Horde?
aliases: what is the horde main city
faq.answer: Orgrimmar is the Horde's fortified capital and its center of government and war. Built into the crags of northern Durotar in Kalimdor, it holds Thrall's throne and enclaves for troll, tauren, and Forsaken delegates.

faq.q: Are the Horde and Alliance actively at war right now?
aliases: are we at war with alliance
faq.answer: The Horde and Alliance live under an uneasy truce made after the Battle of Mount Hyjal. Fights over lumber in Ashenvale, territorial friction in the Alterac Mountains, and old hatred keep both sides in a simmering cold war of local skirmishes.

faq.q: Do all trolls belong to the Horde?
faq.answer: No. The Darkspear tribe is the Horde's main troll member, having sailed to Kalimdor with Thrall. Most other troll tribes across Azeroth are hostile, though groups such as the Revantusk tribe of the Hinterlands keep separate pacts of friendship and mutual defense without formally joining.

angles.text: The New Horde offers your people a path to redemption. Under Thrall's banner, you cast off the legacy of demon blood and reclaim ancestral shamanic honor.
You stood shoulder to shoulder with the orcs in the centaur wars. Together, you preserved your sacred lands in Mulgore and found steadfast spiritual brothers.
Thrall's fleet rescued your Darkspear tribe from destruction on its island home. Your people pledged their spears and shadows to the Horde's survival.
Your place in the Horde shields the Forsaken from the Living who would purge Lordaeron. Many in Kalimdor regard your ways with quiet caution.
To human, dwarven, and elven eyes, the Horde remains a gathering of monstrous savages and treacherous corpses. They believe it cannot keep the peace.
